scope: Read-only source diagnosis; no guest input or source behavior change.

findings.fact: Capture-only opens a new client and saves first nonincremental full framebuffer; settle is only used after input. Full pixel coverage proves completeness, not new guest rendering.
Nonincremental request sets FORCE and client dirty area; it does not wait for a new rendered frame.
With no clients, refresh returns before graphic_hw_update. With clients it updates hardware, copies dirty guest surface and sends updates.
First client recreates server surface and invokes graphic_hw_update before protocol; old VNC server-cache retention is not established as the cause.
Default refresh interval30ms, idle maximum3000ms. Refresh intervals are not guest presentation guarantees.
gfx_update notifies dirty framebuffer rows then raises OUTPUT_READY interrupt; it does not synchronously wait for a new guest-composited frame.
Guest register write0x4602C with bit12 schedules draw bottom half.
Draw bottom half draws both genpipes to console surface and raises FRAME_PROCESSED.

interpretation: A reconnect can observe the current guest surface before the guest reacts to renewed output-ready refresh. This is a source-supported possible mechanism, not attribution of the observed21-second visual discrepancy. App active/callback are lifecycle boundaries, not presentation boundaries.
minimal_host_only_recommendation: Keep same connection alive; retain immediate initial frame, wait bounded configurable settle and issue another nonincremental full request.
Record wall and monotonic request, complete-receive and save times separately; retain both hashes and do not infer freshness from stability alone.
For launch observation, keeping a VNC client connected throughout OPEN avoids re-enabling refresh only at the capture boundary. This still does not synchronize presentation with lifecycle.

runtime_observation_from_parent.qualification: Parent supplied observations; this inspection does not replace their raw capture evidence.
